claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy contains dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Conventionally processed colonies have relatively large lamellar spacing.
Internal boundaries in the conventional microstructure are prone to microcrack initiation under tensile loading.
Rapid solidification can refine the lamellar-colony scale and lamellar spacing.
Rapid solidification will produce a more homogeneous distribution of internal boundaries.
Lamellar-scale refinement reduces the effective length of internal boundaries that act as stress concentrators.
Reducing the effective length of stress-concentrating boundaries suppresses microcrack initiation.
Lamellar refinement enhances room-temperature ductile deformation mechanisms.
The refined microstructure delays the onset of brittle fracture at room temperature.
Rapidly solidified material will have higher yield strength than the conventional baseline.
Rapidly solidified material will have higher ultimate tensile strength than the conventional baseline.
Rapidly solidified material will have greater room-temperature total strain to failure than the conventional baseline.
Conventional processing typically produces coarser lamellar colonies.
The conventional baseline has an inferior strength-ductility combination because microcracks initiate at larger internal boundaries.
Residual stresses or secondary phases generated during rapid solidification may negate the expected mechanical benefits.
Lamellar spacing must reach a critical refinement scale to suppress microcrack initiation.
The quantitative strength and ductility changes depend on refined lamellar spacing and processing-induced defects.
